reviewStandard: The six queued routes fail the pre-generation site, membrane-topology, duplicate-identity, chemical-speciation, redox-compartment, or physiological-state gate. They receive no marked prompt, no generation call, and no raster pending separate review.
promotionRule: No Batch 086 route is eligible for generation or promotion until its documented scope, identity, topology, speciation, compartment, measurement, evidence-tier, or duplicate-route conflicts are corrected and independently re-audited.

routeDecisions.reason: Distinct oral habitats, community members, spatial scales, translocation routes, metals, and systemic associations are merged into one generalized ecosystem.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Split by sampled oral site and define spatial scale, host state, assay, taxonomic resolution, community organization, and evidence-qualified association.

routeDecisions.reason: A general asymmetric membrane is mixed with incorrectly localized transport components and unsupported universal metal-tolerance, disease, and therapeutic claims.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Select one organism/envelope and define both membranes, periplasm, peptidoglycan, outer-leaflet chemistry, named protein topology, transport direction/energy, and phenotype.

routeDecisions.reason: The route duplicates oxalates and overstates organism loss and colonization as causal stone-risk and therapeutic effects without chemical, host, diet, assay, and outcome boundaries.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Merge the canonical record; define chemical species, calcium oxalate, microbial degradation, host transport, urinary crystallization, diet, population, assay, and clinical outcome.

routeDecisions.reason: The duplicate route combines food content, endogenous synthesis, diverse microbial pathways, mineral binding, disease, and interventions while overstating ecological exclusivity.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Merge with oxalate and separate chemical speciation, diet, microbial pathway/taxon, intestinal handling, urine supersaturation, disease endpoint, and intervention evidence.

routeDecisions.reason: Multiple reactive species, compartments, organisms, metals, defenses, biomarkers, diseases, and interventions are collapsed into one universal mechanism.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Split by species and compartment; define exposure, dose/time, redox target/pathway, assay and sample, biomarker specificity, damage endpoint, organism, and evidence tier.

routeDecisions.reason: A colon epithelial gradient hypothesis is generalized across metals, respiration modes, intestinal and extraintestinal diseases, and interventions without measurement or location boundaries.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Define intestinal segment/radial location, host state, oxygen or redox variable, method/time, metabolite flux, organism respiration phenotype, and evidence tier; separate other body sites.
